title: Missing Number

content.problemStatement:
You're given an array containing n distinct numbers, each one taken from the range `[0, n]`. Exactly one number in that range is missing from the array.

**Find and return the missing number.**
constraints: all the numbers of nums are unique
content.inputFormat: A single array of distinct integers nums.
content.outputFormat: Return the single missing integer from range [0, n].

sampleTestCases.explanation: n = 3, so the full range is [0, 3]. 0 and 1 and 3 are present, 2 is missing
n = 2, so the full range is [0, 2]. 0 and 1 are present, 2 is missing

notes: Follow up: Could you implement a solution using only O(1) extra space complexity and O(n) runtime complexity?

solution.approach: cyclic sort: place each value at index value (since values fall in [0, n]), then scan for the index whose value doesn't match

bruteForce.description: Sort the array, then walk through checking that each index matches its expected value.
bruteForce.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(1) space

better.description: Compute expected sum n*(n+1)//2 and subtract actual sum, or use XOR reduction.

optimal.pattern: cyclic sort: place each value at index value (since values fall in [0, n]), then scan for index whose value does not match
optimal.description: Cyclic sort placing each value at its matching index, or Gauss arithmetic sum for single-pass O(1) extra space.

solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra (besides the array copy you return from)

hints: Every value in the array, if it belongs anywhere, belongs at a specific index. What index would value v naturally sit at?

Try walking through the array and, for each position, swapping its value to the index equal to that value, repeating until the current position holds a value that already belongs there or is out of range.
After one pass of cyclic placement, scan through and find the first index i where nums[i] != i - that i is your missing number.
Alternatively, sum the numbers from 0 to n using n * (n + 1) / 2 and subtract the sum of the array.
followUps: Could you implement a solution using only O(1) extra space complexity and O(n) runtime complexity?
learningObjectives: Master cyclic sort placement technique for numbers in range [0, n].
Understand XOR and Gauss summation arithmetic approaches for O(1) space missing element detection.
Guard against array bounds when value equals n.
